before: How Decisions Should Be Made—and How They Actually Are
title: How Decisions Should Be Made—and How They Actually Are
subtitle: A rational benchmark is not a psychological portrait
rationale: Retains the normative/descriptive contrast and the functional decision loop.

title: Building a Better Decision
subtitle: Alternatives, Opportunity Cost, Information, and Robustness
rationale: Names the chapter's workflow for alternatives, opportunity costs, information, and robustness.

title: Limited Attention
subtitle: What Becomes Evidence?
rationale: The core constraint underlying selection, divided attention, and switching; retained from the preceding title revision.

title: The Predictive Mind
subtitle: Perception Is Inference
rationale: Covers perception as inference, priors, prediction error, and precision; generative AI remains optional.

title: Expectations
subtitle: When Predictions Become Causes
rationale: Expectations change forecasts and, through identifiable pathways, outcomes; selective evidence belongs primarily in Chapter 10.

title: Valuation
subtitle: How Options Become Worth Choosing
rationale: Covers emotion, bodily state, self, others, and subjective comparison without listing every value input.

title: The Narrator After Choice
subtitle: Why Reasons Are Not Always Causes
rationale: Keeps the organizing question of retrospective explanation; includes introspection, confabulation, choice blindness, and dissonance.

title: Intuition and Deliberation
subtitle: Fast and Frugal Thinking
rationale: Now names both intuitive and deliberative processing, including expertise and their interaction.

title: Availability, Affect, and Representativeness
subtitle: What Feels Likely
rationale: Retains the requested three mechanisms; dilution is an extension of representativeness.

title: Confirmation Bias and Motivated Reasoning
subtitle: Beliefs That Defend Themselves
rationale: Now explicitly names confirmation bias and motivated reasoning, the chapter's central mechanisms.

title: Anchors, Halos, and Decoys
subtitle: When Context Rewrites Comparison
rationale: Retains the memorable three principal context effects; the subtitle and new evaluation section cover the broader comparison theme.

title: Framing
subtitle: When the Same Facts Become Different Decisions
rationale: Covers equivalent descriptions, memory questions, and communicative framing without an overlong heading.

title: Priming, Fluency, and Familiarity
subtitle: Accessibility, Familiarity, and Ease
rationale: Adds priming to the title because it is a substantial treatment distinct from fluency and familiarity.

title: Base Rates and Updating
subtitle: Base Rates, Conditional Probability, and Bayesian Updating
rationale: Matches conditional probability, reference classes, natural frequencies, and Bayes.

title: Randomness and Overconfidence
subtitle: Samples, Randomness, Regression, and Calibration
rationale: Now makes overconfidence visible alongside sampling, streaks, regression, and calibration; the subtitle retains the statistical scope.

title: Risky Decision Making
subtitle: A Probability Is Not Yet a Feeling
rationale: Covers expected value/utility, risk, ambiguity, compounding-related growth, and decision consequences.

title: Prospect Theory
subtitle: Gains and Losses Begin at a Reference Point
rationale: Matches reference dependence, value and weighting functions, loss aversion, and their boundaries.

title: Decisions From Experience
subtitle: When Rare Events Are Not Encountered
rationale: Matches feedback, rare-event sampling, recency, exploration, and normalization of risk.

title: Intertemporal Decision Making
subtitle: Why Later Loses to Now
rationale: Preserves the specifically requested Intertemporal Decision Making and Why Later Loses to Now subtitle.

title: Mental Accounting
subtitle: Money Is Fungible; Minds Label It
rationale: The common home for labeling, bracketing, payment coupling, sunk cost, and diversification.

title: Habits, Wanting, and Self-Control
subtitle: The past can cue action before the present has finished deciding
rationale: Separates cue-linked habits, motivational attraction, pleasure, and practical self-control.

title: Deciding for a Better Life
subtitle: Satisfaction, Connection, and Meaning
rationale: Spans forecasting, experience, remembered utility, life evaluation, connection, and meaning.

title: Strategic Interdependence
subtitle: The Best Move Depends on Other Minds
rationale: Names the dependence of a best move on others' actions and expectations.

title: Behavioral Game Theory
subtitle: Equilibrium Is a Benchmark, Not a Portrait
rationale: Covers limited strategic depth, equilibrium as benchmark, learning, and evolutionary models.

title: Cooperation and Social Preferences
subtitle: Self-Interest Is Not the Only Payoff
rationale: Separates strategic cooperation from altruism, inequality, intentions, and norms.

title: Social Norms and Conformity
subtitle: When Other People Become Evidence
rationale: Matches social information, conformity, norm expectations, and cascades.

title: Markets, Mispricing, and Bubbles
subtitle: Prices as Social Signals
rationale: Replaces Prices as Social Signals with the full scope: efficiency, arbitrage, mispricing, bubbles, and investor behavior.

title: Authority, Groupthink, and Shared Responsibility
subtitle: Signals that coordinate behavior—and can be counterfeited
rationale: Retains the three mechanisms that organize authority, group information, and bystander responsibility.

title: Culture and Identity
subtitle: The Same Action Is Not the Same Act
rationale: Preserves the main social-meaning argument; personality is a bounded optional lens, not a replacement theme.

title: Persuasion
subtitle: Changing Minds Means Updating Models
rationale: Covers routes, sources, resistance, commitments, self-persuasion, and ethical influence.

title: Why Stories Move Minds
subtitle: Narrative turns information into simulated meaning
rationale: Retains the explanatory focus on attention, identity, emotion, simulation, and identifiable victims.

title: Building an Evidence-Aligned Message
subtitle: Use narrative to carry evidence, not to replace it
rationale: Distinguishes practical message construction from the mechanisms in Chapter 31.

title: Communication
subtitle: Language Is Not a File Transfer
rationale: Keeps the umbrella for grounding, pragmatic inference, projection, and verified understanding.

title: Connection and Repair
subtitle: Warm Honesty Makes Truth Usable
rationale: Covers responsive listening, appreciation, warm honesty, apology, and forgiveness.

title: Negotiation as Joint Decision Design
subtitle: Interdependence turns choice into a shared search
rationale: Names negotiation as preparation, interaction, implementation, and learning; introduces principled negotiation.

title: Distributive Negotiation
subtitle: Preparing and Claiming Value
rationale: Uses the standard course term for alternatives, reservation values, opening offers, concessions, and claiming value.

title: Integrative Negotiation
subtitle: Creating Value Across Differences
rationale: Uses the standard course term for interests, logrolling, differences, and Pareto improvement.

title: Designing Better Agreements
subtitle: Make the promise clear enough to carry out and check
rationale: Names contingent agreements, multiple offers, verification, process, and implementation.

title: Behavior Design
subtitle: Make the Better Action Easier
rationale: Matches the practical workflow and distinguishes design from the contested depleted-resource account.

title: Choice Architecture
subtitle: The Environment Gets a Vote
rationale: Covers menus, defaults, friction, choice overload, feedback, welfare, and governance.

title: Decision Hygiene
subtitle: Build a Process That Can Learn
rationale: Keeps the process focus on independent estimates, noise, disagreement, review, and accountable judgment.

title: Deciding With Data and AI
subtitle: Data Driven Decision Making
rationale: Now explicitly names AI as well as data; the chapter centers on prediction, valuation, causal benefit, and accountable action.
